ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in rectangle $ABCD$, diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at point $E$. $BF \parallel AC$ and $CF \parallel BD$. If the area of quadrilateral $BECF$ is 2, what is the area of the rectangle $ABCD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $BF\parallel AC$ and $CF\parallel BD$, \\
it follows that quadrilateral BECF is a parallelogram, \\
since rectangle ABCD, \\
we have BE=CE, \\
thus, quadrilateral BECF is a rhombus; \\
hence, the area of rhombus BECF, $S_{\text{rhombus} BECF}=2S_{\triangle BEC}=2$, \\
thus, the area of $\triangle BEC=1$; \\
since rectangle ABCD, \\
it follows that the area of rectangle ABCD, $S_{\text{rectangle} ABCD}=4S_{\triangle BEC}=\boxed{4}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in rectangle $ABCD$, diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at point $E$. $BF \parallel AC$ and $CF \parallel BD$. If the area of quadrilateral $BECF$ is 2, what is the area of the rectangle $ABCD$?
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer: Given that $BF\parallel AC$ and $CF\parallel BD$, quadrilateral $BECF$ is a parallelogram. Since $ABCD$ is a rectangle, $BE=CE$, so $BECF$ is a rhombus. Hence $S_{\text{rhombus }BECF}=2S_{\triangle BEC}=2$, so $S_{\triangle BEC}=1$. Therefore, $S_{\text{rectangle }ABCD}=4S_{\triangle BEC}=\boxed{4}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, ABCD is a rectangle, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, and D is at the upper right; the two diagonals AC and BD of the rectangle intersect at the interior point E. Point F is located below BC, and line segments BF and CF together with BE and CE form the lower quadrilateral BECF, which in appearance looks like a rhombus/parallelogram region.

Reasoning: From the given condition BF ∥ AC, and E and C are on AC, so BF ∥ EC; also from CF ∥ BD, and B and E are on BD, so CF ∥ BE. Therefore the two pairs of opposite sides of quadrilateral BECF are respectively parallel, so it is a parallelogram. The diagonal BC of the parallelogram divides it into two triangles of equal area, so S(BECF)=2S(△BEC). It is known that S(BECF)=2, therefore S(△BEC)=1. The two diagonals of a rectangle intersect and bisect each other, dividing the rectangle into four triangles of equal area, one of which is △BEC, so S(ABCD)=4S(△BEC)=4.
